I am 68 this year. I never went to school, not one day. I cannot read a single word. But I have farmed for 48 years, since I was 20 years old. My mother-in-law taught me everything I know about the land. I have 10.1 mu in Quzhou County. I plant 7 mu with wheat and maize — wheat in the winter, then maize in the summer after we cut the wheat. The other 3.1 mu I plant cotton. Cotton is a lot of work, especially all the spraying, but when the price is good it brings more money than grain. My son and his wife work in a factory in Handan and send money home. My husband is 72 and his legs hurt, he cannot bend down anymore. I do most of the farming myself, but my nephew helps me during harvest and when I need to carry heavy bags.

Last year my wheat gave me about 1000 jin per mu. This year I will do the same thing I always do. For the 7 mu of wheat, I put two bags of compound fertilizer and one and a half bags of urea on each mu. The seed dealer says Jimai 502 is a good seed — I have been buying it for many years and it has never let me down. I irrigate four times: once before winter, then in March when the wheat turns green, again when the stems are growing tall, and once more when the grain is filling. I spray insecticide twice — once for the green bugs in spring, once later for the bugs that eat the leaves. I spray herbicide once in early spring, and fungicide once because two years ago my neighbor Old Wang's wheat got a sickness and I don't want that to happen to my field.

For the maize, after we harvest the wheat in early June, we plant the maize directly without plowing. Everyone in our village does this now. It saves time and diesel. I use Denghai 605 hybrid seed. I don't put much extra fertilizer on the maize because the wheat already left food in the ground. I give it half a bag of urea when it is knee-high. I irrigate twice — once when the seedlings are small, and once when the tassels come out. I spray insecticide twice for the corn borer, and herbicide once when the plants are small. Maize does not need fungicide.

Cotton is on 3.1 mu. I plow it with the rotary tiller in late April before planting. I use Guoxinmian cotton seed. Cotton needs a lot of food — I put two bags of compound fertilizer and one bag of urea per mu. I irrigate twice, but carefully — too much water and the cotton grows too tall and does not make bolls. The biggest problem with cotton is insects! I spray 13 times for insects, maybe 14 if the bollworms are bad. Every ten days I have to go out with the sprayer. I also spray herbicide once. If it rains too much I might spray fungicide once, but usually I do not bother.

I worry about costs every day. Urea is more than 100 yuan per bag now. Compound fertilizer is 150 yuan. Every spray costs 20 or 30 yuan for the medicine. Electricity for the well pump is expensive too. But if I cut back on fertilizer and the yield drops, I lose much more money than I save. A bad harvest is a disaster for my family. Wasting a little fertilizer is just a cost. So I keep doing what I did last year. Old Wang has 8 mu and he does almost the same thing. I watch what he does. If he adds more fertilizer, I think about adding more too. Change is risky. Doing what I know is safe.
